decision: not retained in this form: exactness and report preservation pass, but unconditionally rounding the exact MAX width to infinity causes an avoidable 2.86-3.62x scan regression in the saturation control

matched_probe.scope: Five fresh alternating processes per variant/mode on CPU 0 after 100 ms integer-only conditioning. Timing uses the system allocator; memory binaries separately count requested Rust allocations. Each exact full private index implementation is extracted verbatim and linked to its frozen production library; the private bounds wrapper is represented by the public STRICT wrapper. Nine prepared point workloads measure index construction, first, repeated and cloned-point queries. Point producer construction and query clones are outside measurement; selected-point certified equality checks run after measured queries. Independent box-overlap and known-point witnesses check every candidate output, including a conservative false-positive saturation control. Incorrect baseline omissions remain recorded as correctness deltas. This is an index microbenchmark, not complete public Boolean performance or an application speedup claim.

failed_harness_preserved: contact-index-production-cost/failure.json: first cost harness failed compilation because Real has no From<usize>; explicit u32 conversions correct the bounded fixture coordinates. No resource sample ran before the correction.

resource_review.corrected_output_cost: The twelve formerly empty candidate lists now allocate their required output: 32 retained bytes per singleton query or 512 retained bytes for 64 contacts. Five allocation samples repeat exactly.
resource_review.avoidable_saturation: The independently verified source box [0, MAX] has exactly representable width MAX. Unconditional next_up makes it infinity and causes queries to scan 64 additional negative-key boxes. All three saturation query phases regress, with disjoint baseline/candidate sample ranges.
resource_review.other_timing_controls: The full samples and unfavorable ordinary controls are retained; no uniform speedup is claimed.
resource_review.next_candidate: Preserve the exact subtraction for equal endpoints or a zero endpoint; round every remaining width upward. This retains the completeness proof while avoiding unnecessary saturation and zero-width inflation.

next_step: Freeze and validate the refined width calculation in a new production checkout. Repeat the correctness, report and resource gates before admitting any runtime change.
limitations: Direct index microbenchmarks use the exact extracted implementation and actual public production point producers, with the public STRICT bounds wrapper replacing private access. They do not establish full Boolean performance.
The signed-zero adapter failure is a private mathematical-order contract case; actual signed-zero producer reachability is unverified.
No complete public Boolean failure, broad native-stroke admission, full-workspace validation or properties.md completion is claimed.
